papers.title_in_file: Reinforcement Learning in Ultracold Atom Experiments (arXiv 2306.16764v1)
papers.what_it_is: A report of deep reinforcement learning (DDPG) controlling a rubidium magneto-optical trap, trained on the experiment and in simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that an RL agent trained directly on the experiment converged to a cooling scheme resembling molasses cooling, and that the control was trained to be robust against external perturbations.
quotes: As proof-of-concept, we perform training of the agent directly on the experiment, which rapidly converges to a cooling scheme resembling well known molasses cooling.
The machine control is trained to be robust against external perturbations and able to react to situations not seen during the training.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one apparatus and one trap (Abstract, Introduction).
assertions.reader_inference: One rubidium MOT apparatus; no independent replication in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors report that an agent trained on a simulation, when evaluated on the real experiment, showed control that qualitatively mimics its behavior in the simulation, and that they read this as a successful sim-to-real transfer.
quotes: The corresponding control presented in Fig. 4b (right) qualitatively mimics the behavior of the agent evaluated on the simulation and thereby indicates a successful sim-to-real transfer.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical, qualitative result from one study (Results, sim-to-real section).
assertions.reader_inference: The transfer is judged qualitatively from control sequences, not by a stated numerical threshold in this passage.

assertions.value: The authors state that they facilitated convergence of the training to comprehensible control strategies by limiting the number of parameters and their range.
quotes: In this work we have facilitated the convergence of the training to comprehensible control strategies by limiting the number of parameters and their range.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this limit on its own setup (Discussion and Outlook).

assertions.value: The authors report that in the simulated environment, training with only integrated fluorescence signals instead of the full image did not converge to the optimal policy.
quotes: We have conducted tests in the simulated environment providing the agent only with integrated fluorescence signals instead of the full image as observable.
The training in such a scenario did not converge to the optimal policy, in particular, the agent was not able to adapt to any perturbation.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from a simulated test (Methods).

papers.what_it_is: A short note reporting QAOA runs for MaxCut on 3-regular graphs on Quantinuum trapped-ion processors.

assertions.value: The authors report that for all N = 20 MaxCut instances on 3-regular graphs run on the Quantinuum H1-1 processor, solution quality increased monotonically with p up to 10.
quotes: we report a successful execution of QAOA with classically-optimized parameters applied to the MaxCut problem on 3-regular graphs with N = 20
For all N = 20 problem instances considered, we observe that the solution quality obtained by the algorithm increases monotonically with p up to 10.
on the Quantinuum H1-1 and H2 trapped-ion quantum processors.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical hardware result from one study on four instances (Introduction and Results, p.1-2).
assertions.reader_inference: Success is defined by the authors as monotonic improvement in solution quality with p, not as beating a classical solver.

assertions.value: The authors report that at N = 32, using QAOA with fixed parameters not optimized per instance, performance was less consistent, though monotonic improvement with p up to 10 was still observed.
quotes: we extend the experiments to N = 32 by using QAOA with fixed parameters
Due to parameters not being optimized on per-instance basis, we observe less consistent QAOA performance.
Still, at N = 32 we observe monotonic improvement of QAOA performance with p up to 10
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical hardware result from one study (Introduction, p.1).

assertions.value: The authors state that neither the expected cut nor the probability of the optimal solution measurably decreased as layers were added, and that these observations suggest the experiment is not yet limited by the gate fidelity of the device.
quotes: measurably decrease as more layers are added.
Combined, these observations suggest that the current experiment is not yet limited by the gate fidelity of the device.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical observation and the authors' interpretation (Results, p.4).
assertions.reader_inference: The claim holds only for the depths and instances tested.

papers.title_in_file: Five Starter Pieces: Quantum Information Science via Semi-definite Programs (arXiv 2112.08276v3)
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, section 4 state discrimination, section 8 channel capacity examples, section 9 concluding remarks.
papers.what_it_is: A tutorial chapter that formulates five quantum information problems as semi-definite programs, with Python notebooks.

assertions.value: The authors state that the chapter is a brief, self-contained introduction to five fundamental problems in Quantum Information Science that are well suited to be formulated as semi-definite programs.
quotes: this chapter presents a brief, self-contained introduction to five fundamental problems in Quantum Information Science (QIS) that are especially well-suited to be formulated as Semi-definite Programs (SDP).
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope in the Abstract, p.1.

assertions.value: The authors state that the optimum value of the state discrimination SDP is often called the Helstrom bound, and that in general this SDP cannot be solved analytically but numerical SDP solvers can be used.
quotes: The optimum value is often called the Helstrom bound [41]. In general, the SDP in (59) cannot be solved analytically; however, one can use numerical SDP solvers.
assertions.certainty_reason: Attributed to earlier work (Helstrom, cited as [41]); the chapter restates it.

assertions.value: The authors state that practical use of SDPs for QIS can easily become numerically intractable for current solvers as the number of quantum systems involved increases, and that this can make the SDPs of several problems intractable for larger k.
quotes: However, practical use of SDPs for QIS can easily become numerically intractable for current solvers as the number of quantum systems involved increase
This can make the SDPs in Secs. 4,5,6, and 7 numerically intractable for larger k.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state this limit in the Concluding Remarks, p.29.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum transport in randomized quantum graphs (arXiv 2404.09106v2)
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results and ending comments.
papers.what_it_is: A theoretical physics paper on transmission coefficients of open quantum graphs with randomly removed edges.
papers.why_not: The paper studies wave transport in open quantum graphs as a physics problem. It describes no quantum computing, quantum machine learning, machine learning, finance or evaluation-method result.

papers.title_in_file: An Introduction to Quantum Machine Learning for Engineers (arXiv 2205.09510v4)
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, contents, chapter 6 introduction, section 6.2, the barren-plateau passage, section 6.11 conclusions. Chapters 1 to 5 background not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: A monograph introducing quantum machine learning with parametrized quantum circuits, VQE, and generative and supervised models.

assertions.value: The author states that the monograph provides a self-contained introduction to quantum machine learning for engineers with a background in probability and linear algebra, covering parametrized quantum circuits, the variational quantum eigensolver, and unsupervised and supervised formulations.
quotes: This monograph provides a self-contained introduction to quantum machine learning for an audience of engineers with a background in probability and linear algebra.
Then, it covers parametrized quantum circuits, the variational quantum eigensolver, as well as unsupervised and supervised quantum machine learning formulations.
assertions.certainty_reason: The monograph states its own scope in the Abstract.

assertions.value: The author states that gradient-based optimization for PQCs is significantly less efficient than for standard machine learning models, because estimating the gradient entails a complexity that scales linearly with the number of model parameters.
quotes: Gradient-based optimization for PQCs is significantly less efficient than its counterpart for standard machine learning models.
In fact, estimating the gradient entails a complexity that scales linearly with the number of model parameters.
assertions.certainty_reason: Expository statement in the chapter conclusions (Section 6.11, p.217), not a proof in the quoted passage.

assertions.value: The author states that proving quantum advantages is possible for very specific problems, but that current practice appears to rely on limited comparisons via heuristic arguments and experiments, or on sidestepping the question of quantum advantages.
quotes: While it is possible to prove such advantages for very specific problems,
the current practice appears to be that of making limited comparisons via heuristic arguments and experiments, or by sidestepping the question of
assertions.certainty_reason: The author's characterization of the field, without a survey in the quoted passage (Section 6.11, p.217).

assertions.value: The author states that it has been shown that when the ansatz is sufficiently rich and the parameters are randomly initialized, the partial derivatives of the cost tend exponentially to zero in probability as n grows, a phenomenon known as the barren plateaus problem.
quotes: it has been shown that, when the ansatz is sufficiently rich and the model parameters are randomly initialized, the partial derivatives tend exponentially to zero in probability as n grows. This is known as the barren plateaus problem.
assertions.certainty_reason: Attributed to prior work (barren plateaus, cited in Section 6.12); not derived here.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum walk on simplicial complexes for simplicial community detection (arXiv 2401.00699v3)
papers.what_it_is: A proposal of a discrete-time quantum walk algorithm for detecting simplicial communities, tested on Zachary's karate club network.

assertions.value: The author states that the paper presents a quantum walk algorithm to detect higher-order community structures called simplicial communities, using the Fourier coin to produce entangled translation states among adjacent simplices.
quotes: we present a quantum walk algorithm to detect higher-order community structures called simplicial communities.
We utilize the Fourier coin to produce entangled translation states among adjacent simplices in a simplicial complex.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own method in the Abstract.

assertions.value: The author reports that on Zachary's karate club network, 45 triangles (2-simplices) are clustered into four 2-down communities, one of which is an isolated 2-simplex.
quotes: N2 = 45 triangles (2-simplices) are clustered into four 2-down communities, one of which is an isolated 2-simplex
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on one small network (Section 5).
assertions.reader_inference: A single small test case; the paper gives no classical or quantum-hardware comparison in this passage.

assertions.value: The author states that the algorithm was only tested on one network and needs to be validated through various examples and mathematical proof.
quotes: Although the proposed quantum walk algorithm was only tested on
it needs to be validated through various examples and mathematical proof
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this limit in Sections 5 and 6.

papers.title_in_file: Theory and Implementation of the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (arXiv 2301.09535v1)
papers.partial_detail: Overview, structure, Notebook 4 results (sections 4.5 and 4.6). Notebooks 1 to 3 and appendices skimmed only.
papers.what_it_is: A tutorial with Qiskit code and experiments on the 27-qubit IBM computer ibmq_ehningen.

assertions.value: The author states that the tutorial gives a comprehensible introduction to the theory and implementation of QAOA, and that it provides extensive experiments on the 27 qubit quantum computer ibmq_ehningen.
quotes: The present tutorial aims to provide a comprehensible and easily accessible introduction into the theory and implementation of the famous Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA).
we provide extensive experiments on the 27 qubits state-of-the-art quantum computer ibmq_ehningen.
assertions.certainty_reason: The tutorial states its own scope in the Overview, p.1.

assertions.value: The author reports that for one example the QAOA circuits for p = 2 were too deep for ibmq_ehningen so that no meaningful result could be obtained, and that all examples of Example Series 2 had CNOT counts too high for current quantum computers.
quotes: The QAOA circuits for p = 2 are too deep for ibmq_ehningen so that no meaningful result can be obtained
For all examples of Example Series 2 we are in regimes of number of CNOT gates that are too high for current quantum computers.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one device on specific problem instances (Section 4.5).
assertions.reader_inference: The limit is for this device and these examples in 2022, not for QAOA in general.

assertions.value: The author reports that error rates of quantum computers change significantly over time, with a drastic effect on result quality on ibmq_ehningen, and recommends running experiments on a series of different dates and, if possible, on different quantum computers.
quotes: The error rates of quantum computers are not static but significantly change over time.
In the following figures we observe that this has a drastic effect on the quality of the results obtained from ibmq_ehningen.
we recommend running experiments on a series of different dates and (if possible) on different quantum computers.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical observation from one device (Section 4.5.3).

papers.title_in_file: Toward Automated Quantum Variational Machine Learning (arXiv 2312.01567v1)
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, simulation results, failed attempts, conclusions.
papers.what_it_is: A paper proposing MUSE, a multi-locality search for initial points and parameters of quantum variational circuits, evaluated by simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that, in simulations with five real-world classification datasets, MUSE improves the detection accuracy of quantum variational classifiers 2.3 times on average with respect to the observed lowest scores.
quotes: Simulations with five real-world classification datasets indicate that on average, MUSE improves the detection accuracy of quantum variational classifiers 2.3 times with respect to the observed lowest scores.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation result from one study (Abstract; Section IV).
assertions.reader_inference: The baseline is the lowest score seen during the search, not a typical or tuned baseline, so the 2.3 times figure overstates the gain over a sensible default.

assertions.value: The authors report that the classification and regression scores of quantum variational models trained with MUSE are on par with the classical counterparts.
quotes: Furthermore, the classification and regression scores of the quantum variational models trained with MUSE are on par with the classical counterparts.
We clearly see that the QVCs trained with MUSE achieve accuracy performances that are on par with the classical classifiers.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation result from one study (Section IV).

assertions.value: The authors report that, applied to two real-world regression datasets, MUSE improves the quality of the predictions from negative coefficients of determination to positive ones.
quotes: when applied to two realworld regression datasets, MUSE improves the quality of the predictions from negative coefficients of determination to positive ones.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation result from one study (Abstract).

assertions.value: The authors state that they could not run MUSE on real IBM quantum hardware for lack of funding, so the results come from simulations.
quotes: In the future, we plan to use the IBM quantum devices to perform simulations with MUSE on real hardware.
Due to lack of funding, we could not perform such simulations.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this limit in Section VI.
